speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have multiple skin lesions; can you tell me how long you have had them and if they are itchy or painful?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential and ESR.
REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide close-up photographs of the skin lesions, noting any changes in size, color, or appearance over time.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: WBC: 6,000 /μL, Hemoglobin: 12 g/dL, Platelets: 300,000 /μL. ESR: NORMAL READINGS.

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The description of skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication is highly suggestive of Molluscum Contagiosum. Given the distribution on the abdomen and extremities, do you have anyone at home or at school who has a similar rash?

REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide clear, close-up photographs of the lesions to confirm the presence of central umbilication and assess for viral warts or folliculitis.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Previously healthy, up-to-date immunizations, no significant illnesses. Social history: Attends daycare three times per week.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The history of attending daycare aligns with the highly contagious nature of the lesions you described. Given your otherwise healthy status and the classic "pearly papules with central umbilication," are there any specific areas of your body where the lesions are most concentrated or clustered?

REQUEST IMAGES: Please ensure the photographs clearly show the umbilicated center of the papules.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum Contagiosum
